hypothesis: An attacker crafts a legacy JWT with ver omitted, string formatted, negative, or malformed, causing int(payload.get('ver') or 1) to bypass db_ver > 1 rotation guard or raise unhandled 500 error.

On unrotated accounts (db_ver == 1), an attacker with a legacy UUID and a single valid token can repeatedly exchange it via /session to obtain brand new 90-day tokens indefinitely, effectively negating token expiration.
A malicious script running in the DOM can dispatch a synthetic tabiji:session_reauth_required event with custom reason text, inducing user phishing to extract the tbj_rec key into the modal.

When user clicks 'Dismiss (Stay Offline)', dismissReauthPrompt sets a 5000ms cooldown during which subsequent legit 401s fail silently; if background sync retries during this window, pending outbox items could be evicted or discarded.

Retaining the session token across 401 until exchange failure causes the invalid token to remain in localStorage if the network drops (e.g. 503 or offline) during exchange, violating fail-closed zero-token storage policy.
